statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-69651 (GHSA-3rxq-g8rj-r2cf) is a .NET denial of service issue in XML processing (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml): crafted signed or encrypted XML can cause excessive work. Microsoft lists the .NET 10 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3rxq-g8rj-r2cf, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/449, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135698, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. Implementation copies of System.Private.Xml.dll are in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework (dotnet10-runtime, the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and the runtime archives it carries) and in the runtime and NativeAOT runtime packs, and every one carries the build's own .NET version. Implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll are in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework (aspnetcore10-runtime and dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap), the ASP.NET Core runtime pack and runtime archive, the SDK's own and F# directories, and, in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml nupkg, the ASP.NET Core and WindowsDesktop transport nupkg files and the Arcade SDK and Build.Tasks.Feed build-tool nupkg files. Each carries the build's own .NET version, except the two build-tool copies (Arcade SDK and Build.Tasks.Feed): in the aarch64 10.0.13-r0 build they are the unfixed 10.0.10 version, and in 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0 they are the fixed 10.0.13 version. So every implementation copy in the first 9 builds (10.0.2-r0 to 10.0.10-r0) is unfixed, 10.0.13-r0 is fixed except for those aarch64 build-tool copies, and 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0 carry the fix in every copy; 10.0.13-r0 therefore reads as affected. The remaining copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. The range ends at 10.0.14-r0, the first published build in which every implementation copy on both architectures is 10.0.13 or later.

CVE-2026-69651 (GHSA-3rxq-g8rj-r2cf) is a .NET denial of service issue in signed XML processing in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml; the fix adds input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibits DTD processing by default, validates entity references and caps the attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms. Microsoft lists the .NET 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3rxq-g8rj-r2cf, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/449, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships System.Private.Xml.dll at its own .NET version, in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap and in that version's runtime pack and NativeAOT compiler pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap; every implementation copy of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll also carries the build's own version: in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, in that SDK's own tools and F# directories, in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and in the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml nupkg and the ASP.NET Core and Windows desktop transport nupkgs in dotnet8-runtime-artifacts; the other copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll are reference assemblies with no implementation code. So the copies are 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 in the first seven builds and 8.0.32 or later from 8.0.32-r0 on. The range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-69651 (GHSA-3rxq-g8rj-r2cf) is a .NET denial of service issue in signed XML processing (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml): crafted XML can make signature, decryption and canonicalization work grow without bound. Microsoft's fix adds input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibits DTD processing by default, validates entity references, bounds encrypted-data processing and caps the attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms. Microsoft lists the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3rxq-g8rj-r2cf, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/449, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135698, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The .NET 10 fix is dotnet/dotnet commit 4b30c96e6e24bd0fa8dc60bfa0e437a2364331fb on release/10.0.1xx ('Signed CMS and Signed XML fixes (10B)'), which changes XmlTextReaderImpl in System.Private.Xml and the canonicalization, decryption, transform and SignedXml code in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml (it also carries signed CMS changes in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs); it is in the v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/4b30c96e6e24bd0fa8dc60bfa0e437a2364331fb. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 10 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source and published in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-28, 10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-10 and dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives each dotnet-sdk-10 build holds (seven in 10.0.301-0 to 10.0.302-1, eight from 10.0.400-1 on). The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-10 build carries one implementation copy of System.Private.Xml.dll, in the .NET runtime shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>, and three implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll: one in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, and two identical copies in the SDK directory /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version> and its FSharp directory. All are managed .NET assemblies. It also carries a reference assembly of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref/<version>, with no implementation code. No other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. We also read the type definitions of every managed assembly, including those inside the nupkg archives, in the amd64 10.0.401-1, 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.404-1 builds and the 10.0.402-0 builds for both architectures: only these copies and the reference assembly define SignedXml, EncryptedXml or CanonicalXml, NuGet.Build.Tasks.Pack.dll does not contain this code, and the only other type in the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml namespace is the X509IssuerSerial structure in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll. The System.Private.Xml.dll copy and the ASP.NET Core System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll copy are byte-identical, on each architecture, to the same files in Microsoft's Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime and Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime linux-x64 or linux-arm64 packages of the same version, and the SDK copies are builds of the same version: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. Every one of these copies records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from: the v10.0.109 to v10.0.112 tags in the builds up to 10.0.401-1, and the v10.0.113, v10.0.114 and v10.0.115 tags from 10.0.402-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The settings the fix adds are present from 10.0.13 on and absent before: System.Private.Xml.dll contains the switch name Switch.System.Xml.DisableOptimizedXmlTextReaderAttributeBufferInvalidation only in the 10.0.13 to 10.0.15 copies, and each of the three implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll contains System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.DangerousMaxCanonicalizationAttributesPerElement, CryptoXmlAllowDtdProcessing and DangerousMaxDecryptionCount only from 10.0.402-0 on (we searched every copy in every build; the existing setting System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.DangerousMaxRecursionDepth is found in every implementation copy; the reference assembly holds none of these strings). The range ends at 10.0.402-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 10 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source and published in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-28, 10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-10 and dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives each dotnet-sdk-10 build holds (seven in 10.0.301-0 to 10.0.302-1, eight from 10.0.400-1 on). The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-10 build carries one implementation copy of System.Private.Xml.dll, in the .NET runtime shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>, and three implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll: one in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, and two identical copies in the SDK directory /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version> and its FSharp directory. All are managed .NET assemblies. It also carries a reference assembly of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref/<version>, with no implementation code. No other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. We also read the type definitions of every managed assembly, including those inside the nupkg archives, in the amd64 10.0.401-1, 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.404-1 builds and the 10.0.402-0 builds for both architectures: only these copies and the reference assembly define SignedXml, EncryptedXml or CanonicalXml, NuGet.Build.Tasks.Pack.dll does not contain this code, and the only other type in the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml namespace is the X509IssuerSerial structure in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll. The System.Private.Xml.dll copy and the ASP.NET Core System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll copy are byte-identical, on each architecture, to the same files in Microsoft's Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime and Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime linux-x64 or linux-arm64 packages of the same version, and the SDK copies are builds of the same version: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. Every one of these copies records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from: the v10.0.109 to v10.0.112 tags in the builds up to 10.0.401-1, and the v10.0.113, v10.0.114 and v10.0.115 tags from 10.0.402-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The settings the fix adds are present from 10.0.13 on and absent before: System.Private.Xml.dll contains the switch name Switch.System.Xml.DisableOptimizedXmlTextReaderAttributeBufferInvalidation only in the 10.0.13 to 10.0.15 copies, and each of the three implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll contains System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.DangerousMaxCanonicalizationAttributesPerElement, CryptoXmlAllowDtdProcessing and DangerousMaxDecryptionCount only from 10.0.402-0 on (we searched every copy in every build; the existing setting System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.DangerousMaxRecursionDepth is found in every implementation copy; the reference assembly holds none of these strings). The range ends at 10.0.402-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
